title: Working with Data: Weighted Means, Dot Plots & Extremes
description: Explore essential mathematical concepts through carefully crafted questions. Strengthen your understanding, practice your reasoning, and learn at your own pace.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate whether a described sampling method is likely to introduce bias.
questions.question: A company surveys every 10th customer who exits the store, regardless of who they are, to estimate customer satisfaction. What can be said about this sampling method?

options.label: A
options.text: The sampling method is reasonably representative of the population

options.label: B
options.text: The sampling method is biased toward frequent shoppers only

options.label: C
options.text: The sample cannot be used because it excludes online customers

questions.explanation: In this scenario, this is a reasonably representative systematic sample of the store's customers, which affects whether the results can be generalized to the full population.
questions.hint: Consider whether every member of the population had a fair and equal chance of being included.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate a weighted mean using given weights and values.
questions.question: A student's final grade is weighted as follows: exam 1 (\(40\%\)) score \(75\), exam 2 (\(30\%\)) score \(69\), and project (\(30\%\)) score \(78\). What is the student's weighted average grade?
questions.explanation: Multiply each score by its weight and sum: \(75 \times 0.40 + 69 \times 0.30 + 78 \times 0.30 = 74.1\).
questions.hint: Multiply each score by its weight (as a decimal), then add the results together.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the mean from data represented in a dot plot.
questions.question: A dot plot shows the number of pets owned by \(6\) students: \(10, 1, 7, 9, 2, 4\). What is the mean number of pets per student?
questions.explanation: Sum the values: \(10 + 1 + 7 + 9 + 2 + 4 = 33\). Divide by the number of students: \(\frac{33}{6} = 5.5\).
questions.hint: Add up all the dots' values and divide by the total number of students.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the minimum value in a data set.
questions.question: What is the minimum value in the following test scores: \(81, 56, 68, 23, 10\)?
questions.explanation: Comparing all the values, the minimum value in the data set is \(10\).
questions.hint: Scan through the data set to find the smallest number.

questions.learningObjective: Evaluate whether a described sampling method is likely to introduce bias.
questions.question: A radio station asks listeners to call in and vote on their favorite song to estimate the preferences of the entire city. What can be said about this sampling method?

options.label: A
options.text: The sampling method is biased and may not represent the full population

options.label: B
options.text: The sampling method is perfectly random and unbiased

options.label: C
options.text: The sample size is too large to be useful

questions.explanation: In this scenario, the sample is biased because it only includes people who listen to that station and choose to call in, which affects whether the results can be generalized to the full population.
questions.hint: Consider whether every member of the population had a fair and equal chance of being included.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish between a population and a sample in a real-world data collection scenario.
questions.question: A researcher measures the height of 40 randomly chosen students out of a school of 500. Does this describe a population or a sample?

options.label: C
options.text: neither a population nor a sample

questions.explanation: Because only a subset of the full group is measured, this data set represents a sample drawn from a larger population.
questions.hint: A population includes every member of the group; a sample includes only part of it.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate a relative frequency as a percentage from a frequency table.
questions.question: A survey of 31 people asked their favorite color, with results: Red: 4; Blue: 5; Green: 12; Yellow: 10. What percentage of respondents chose Green, the most popular color? Round to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: The frequency for Green is \(12\) out of \(31\) total respondents. The percentage is \(\frac{12}{31} \times 100\% \approx 38.7\%\).
questions.hint: Divide the frequency of the category by the total number of respondents, then multiply by 100.
